tagline: Leading U.S. homebuilder and mortgage banking services provider
hero_kpi_rationale: Gross margin is the key KPI for the residential homebuilding sector. It reflects NVR's ability to maintain profitability amid pricing pressures and rising construction costs.
company_description: NVR, Inc. operates as a homebuilder in the United States. The company operates through Homebuilding and Mortgage Banking segments. It engages in the construction and sale of single-family detached homes, townhomes, and condominium buildings under the Ryan Homes, NVHomes, and Heartland Homes names. The company markets its Ryan Homes products to first-time and first-time move-up buyers; and NVHomes and Heartland Homes products to move-up and luxury buyers. It also provides various mortgage related services to its homebuilding customers, as well as brokers title insurance; performs title searches; and sells mortgage loans to investors in the secondary markets on a servicing released basis. The company primarily serves Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Delaware, Washington, D.C., New Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, Western Pennsylvania, Indiana, Illinois, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Florida, Georgia, and Kentucky. NVR, Inc. was founded in 1948 and is headquartered in Reston, Virginia.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after paying direct construction costs.
kpis.description: Homebuilding gross margin declined from 23.7% in 2024 to 21.2% in 2025, impacted by a weak demand environment and community adjustments.
kpis.signal: Margin under pressure in 2025 due to price adjustments in a tight market.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from home sales and mortgage services.
kpis.description: Total homebuilding revenue decreased from $10,292.425M in 2024 to $10,094.269M in 2025, down 2%, primarily due to a 4% drop in units settled.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in 2025 despite stable prices, driven by fewer homes sold.

kpis.name: Home Settlements (units)
kpis.explanation: Number of homes completed and sold during the year.
kpis.description: Settlements declined 4% in 2025 (21,915 units) after rising in 2024 (22,836 units), reflecting a slowdown in demand.
kpis.signal: Fourth consecutive year of growth followed by a decline in 2025.

kpis.name: New Orders (units)
kpis.explanation: Number of new homes ordered by buyers.
kpis.description: New orders fell 10% in 2025 (20,410 units) compared to 22,560 in 2024, indicating deteriorating demand.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2025, signaling weak buyer confidence.

kpis.name: Backlog (units)
kpis.explanation: Number of homes sold but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog declined 15% in units (8,448 units in 2025 versus 9,953 in 2024), reflecting the drop in new orders.
kpis.signal: Backlog sharply lower, a warning sign for future revenues.

kpis.name: Backlog (value)
kpis.explanation: Total value of homes sold but not yet delivered.
kpis.description: Backlog value dropped from $4,791.870M in 2024 to $4,008.043M in 2025, down 16%, linked to fewer orders and lower average prices.
kpis.signal: Backlog declining in both value and volume, pressuring 2026 revenues.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all costs and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income fell 20% in 2025 to $1,339.816M, hurt by lower margins and volumes.
kpis.signal: Sharp earnings decline in 2025, more pronounced than revenue drop.

risks.title: High interest rates affecting demand
risks.summary: High interest rates reduce mortgage affordability, which decreases demand for new homes and negatively impacts sales and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned repeatedly in the 10-K with strong language ("material adverse effect"). It is central to profitability and demand, and its severity is amplified by dependence on credit affordability. The Macro category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Limited access to mortgage financing
risks.summary: Difficulty for customers or buyers of their homes in obtaining mortgage financing can lead to cancellations and reduce demand for NVR homes.
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes that nearly all customers depend on mortgage credit. A tightening of credit conditions is presented as potentially having a "material adverse effect" directly on sales and cash flows. The language is urgent and repeated.

risks.title: Real estate inventory impairment
risks.summary: A decline in land or home inventory values can result in significant losses and reduce profit margins.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well documented with mention of potential losses via forfeited deposits and impairments. The language is concerned but less alarming than for macro risks. This is a key structural risk in the real estate sector.

risks.title: Increased competition in construction and credit
risks.summary: NVR faces strong competition on prices, location, and services, which may limit its ability to grow or maintain margins.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned for both main business lines (construction and credit). The language indicates pressure on prices, quality, and incentives, with an impact on profitability. Less existential than macro risks.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and data breaches
risks.summary: A security breach could lead to leaks of sensitive data, lawsuits, fines, and damage to the company's reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The text describes active security measures but acknowledges persistent vulnerabilities. Mention of severe legal, financial, and reputational consequences. The risk is rising with AI but still moderate compared to economic risks.

risks.title: Materials or labor shortages
risks.summary: Shortages of materials or skilled workers can delay construction and increase costs, affecting profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly identified with reference to delays and increased costs. The language is concerned but not alarmist. It fits within a context of margin pressure but not an existential threat.

risks.title: Mortgage loan repurchase obligations
risks.summary: If originated mortgage loans do not meet investor standards, NVR may have to repurchase them or provide indemnification, resulting in significant losses.
risks.score_rationale: The text warns of significant losses if loans sold in the secondary market do not meet guarantees. The risk is linked to penalties, repurchases, or indemnities, with strong language ("material adverse effect"). Highly specific to the mortgage business.

ai_positioning.summary: NVR does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.

events.title: NVR (NYSE:NVR) Reports Sales Below Analyst Estimates In Q1 CY2026 Earnings
events.body: Homebuilder NVR (NYSE:NVR) missed Wall Street's revenue expectations in Q1 CY2026, with sales falling 21.7% year on year to $1.88 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $67.76 per share was 14.4% below analysts' consensus estimates.
